Scenario: Your dad spends some time during Christmas Eve on his phone. You wonder if he’s bored or unhappy. He might just be answering work messages, and you feel understanding.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel understanding thinking your dad might just be answering work messages?

Scenario: Your dad seems frustrated when you come home from school. He only gives you short answers when you try to talk to him at dinner. You think he is probably reacting this way because he is tired.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your dad's short answers are probably because he's tired?

Scenario: Your dad looks serious when he asks about your curfew. You think he doesn’t trust you anymore. You realize he's probably just worried and trying to keep you safe, and you feel supported.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your dad no longer trusts you?

Scenario: Your dad frowns while checking the mail and sets an envelope aside. You worry it’s another bill and that money’s getting tight. You consider it also might just be a flyer or junk mail, and you feel your stress ease.
Comprehension Question: You think your family fiances are...
Correct Response: Not something you are in charge of worrying about
Incorrect Response: Something you need to know all the details of

Scenario: You're walking upstairs to your room, thinking about seeeing if your older sister wants to play a board game. As you approach her room, she quickly closes the door. While the action is suprusing, you think she's probably looking for privacy.
Comprehension Question: You think your older sister wanting privacy is...
Incorrect Response: A sign she is mad at you

Scenario: You’re telling your aunt a funny story while she scrolls on her phone. You feel hurt by her lack of focus, and wonder if what you’re saying matters. You keep sharing your story, and the worry decreases over time.
Comprehension Question: Does your worry decrease as you keep sharing your story?

Scenario: You’re sitting next to your parent on the couch watching a tv show. You parent is checking their phone, and all of the sudden sighs loudly. You think they are probably frustrated with something they read on their phone.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your parent's sigh is probably about something they read on their phone?

Scenario: You're in your room working on homework when you hear your parents arguing downstairs. Their voices start to rise, and you hear them say your name. You don't like to hear yelling, but you also realize that it is not your fault.
Comprehension Question: Do you realize the argument between your parents isn't your fault?

Scenario: You’re getting ready at the same time as your sibling before leaving the house. You both go to use the bathroom at the same time and they snap at you before locking themselves inside. You feel hurt, but think they are probably lashing out due to anxiety.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your sibling is probably lashing out due to their own anxiety?

Scenario: You’re doing a hard piece of homework at the dining table one evening. All of the sudden, your sibling starts playing loud music that distracts you from your task. When you think about telling your sibling to turn the music down, you think they will be understanding.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your sibling will be understanding if you ask them to turn down the music?

Scenario: You want to talk to someone about your plans for the future, but you don't think your parents will understand what you're worried about. You consider going to your mentor for advice, but you've never asked them for advice before. When you think about their reaction, you think they will probably be encouraging.
Comprehension Question: Do you expect your mentor to react negatively to your request for advice?

Scenario: You walk past the kitchen and hear your parent mention bills while staring at the laptop screen. Out of nowhere, you begin to wonder if your sports fees or school supplies add financial pressure. You remind yourself that you don't know the full picture and managing the family finances isn't your responsibility.
Comprehension Question: Do you remind yourself that managing family finances isn't your responsibility?

Scenario: You invite your mentor to a school event this weekend. You're the only one of your friends with a mentor and are unsure of how others will perceive you. As you get ready for the event, you feel happy.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel happy about inviting your mentor to the event?

Scenario: You hear your parents laughing with your cousin in the other room. You feel a flash of hurt, wondering if they like your cousin more than you. You consider the liklehood of this thought, and you feel unbothered by it.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your parents like your cousin more than you?

Scenario: You are racing to make breakfast before school and in your haste you break one of your mom's favorite mugs. You feel really guilty and anxious about how your mom is going to react when she gets home from work. You know that even if she is upset, she will forgive you.
Comprehension Question: Do you know that your mom will eventually forgive you for breaking the mug?

Scenario: You are about to attend a family dinner with relatives you don’t see often. As you approach the restaurant, you feel your stomach twist into knots. You think this feeling means you are pleased to see your family.
Comprehension Question: Do you interpret your stomach twist as excitement to see your family?

Scenario: You and your dad have a major argument one night. The next morning, your dad leaves early in the morning without saying goodbye. You feel hurt, but remind yourself that your dad loves you and is probably just running late.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your dad left without saying goodbye because he doesn't love you?

Scenario: You and your dad are stuck in a lot of traffic on the way to your sports game. Your dad seems really irritated and keeps making comments about wasted time. You think he is upset with the situation.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your dad's irritation is about the traffic rather than about you?

Scenario: While packing for a holiday trip, your parent double-checks your bag and asks if you remembered everything. You wonder if they think you’re careless or unprepared. You remind yourself they always double-check before trips, and are being thoughtful.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your parent double-checks your bag because they're being thoughtful?

Scenario: One of your chores is to feed the family cat after school. One day, she eats slower than usual and you worry something is wrong. You remind yourself that animal behavior can change for many reasons, and feel anxious as you plan to monitor her eating for a few days.
Comprehension Question: Can a pet's eating habits change for many harmless reasons?

Scenario: Every Monday you call your grandmother to say hello. Today is Monday, and she did not pick up the phone when you called, which is unusual. Your grandmother probably did not answer the phone because she is busy.
Comprehension Question: Is your grandmother probably just busy rather than in trouble?

Scenario: During family photos, your uncle makes a comment about how you’ve changed. You suddenly feel self-conscious. You realize he probably meant it kindly, and you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel confident once you realize your uncle likely meant his comment kindly?

Scenario: During a long holiday visit, your sibling keeps disappearing to their room instead of hanging out with everyone. You worry they’re avoiding you because of something you said earlier. You remind yourself people need breaks, and you feel understanding.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your sibling is avoiding you because of something you said?

Scenario: At dinner, your parent asks how school is going. You respond, and there is a long awkward silence. As it streteches on your begin to feel somewhat uncomfortable. You think your parent is quiet because they are distracted.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your parent's silence at dinner is due to distraction rather than anger?

Scenario: At dinner, your grandparent asks detailed questions about your classes. As you speak, they listen closely without reacting much. You think their lack of reaction means they are focused.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your grandparent's quiet listening means they're focused on you?

Scenario: At a family event, someone jokes about you being “the responsible one" of your siblings. You feel a flash of anxiety, wondering if that means you’re expected to handle everything while your siblings get off easy. You consider that responsibility should be shared fairly.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe you alone are expected to handle all the responsibility?

Scenario: After your game, your dad is quiet during the drive home. You assume he’s disappointed that your team lost. He might just be giving you space to cool off, and you start to feel better.
Comprehension Question: Do you start to feel better once you consider your dad just needed space to cool off?

Scenario: After your competition, your mom says, “You’ll do better next time.” You hear it as criticism at first, but then you realize she probably meant it kindly. You feel supported.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel supported once you realize your mom meant her comment kindly?

Scenario: After a tough loss, you slump into the car feeling like you ruined everything. You brace for disappointment as silence fills the ride. As your parent quietly passes you a snack without saying much, you remember that support can be quiet too, and that you are still loved.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your parent's silence in the car means they've stopped caring?

Scenario: A relative makes a neutral comment about your apperance changing since last year. You instantly feel inscure, worried they mean the observation in a critical way. When you think about how you choose to dress and present yourself, you feel happy with your choices.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel happy with how you choose to dress and present yourself?

Scenario: A disagreement at home ends ends in everyone storming away to their own rooms. Sitting in your, you worry the silence means something bigger is wrong. You remind yourself that sometimes people need time alone to cool off.
Comprehension Question: Do you remind yourself that people sometimes need time alone to cool off?

Scenario: A chore list is taped to the fridge with your name on it. You worry you’re being singled out for not helping enough. You remind yourself chores rotate through the family and your parents are reminding you.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe you're the only one responsible for chores in the family?

Scenario: You overhear your parents talking quietly about how the political situation in the country will affect their jobs. Your stomach drops as you imagine everything changing for your family. When you think about navigating changes together, you feel secure in your family's ability to weather new situations.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel secure in your family's ability to weather new situations together?

Scenario: While visiting extended family, everyone seems busy with their own conversations. You worry you’re supposed to jump in more but don’t know how. You remind yourself being quiet is allowed.
Comprehension Question: Is it okay to stay quiet during family conversations?

Scenario: Your dad coughs a lot one night and looks pale the next morning. As you make breakfast, you beging to worry that he's caught something bad. You consider the liklehood that he's sick with something serious is low.
Comprehension Question: Is it likely that your dad is seriously sick?

Scenario: Your sibling gets into their first-choice college. You feel a sting of jealousy while congratulating them. You remind yourself that your path is still forming, and you feel grounded.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel grounded remembering your own path is still forming?

Scenario: Your family ends up traveling the same weekend as prom, and you can’t change it. You assume you’ll be the only one without prom photos to look back, and you feel a pang of sadness. When you think about your other good memories from high school, you feel grateful.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel grateful for your other good memories from high school?

Scenario: You finally get your driver’s license and ask your dad to borrow the family car to drive to the movies. As your dad hands you the keys, he looks tense and nervous. As you walk to the car, you think that his reaction to you driving alone for the first time is understandable.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your dad's nervousness means he doesn't trust you?

Scenario: Someone in your grade posts a picture of the car their parents got them for their 16th birthday. Your family shares a single car, and your parents would not be able to afford to buy another one. You think about the thoughtful gifts your parents have given you over the years, and you feel grateful for your family.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel grateful for the thoughtful gifts your parents have given you?

Scenario: Someone asks about your college plans, and you hesitate before saying you’re not going. You brace for judgment. Then they just nod and talk about gap years, and you begin to feel oddly relieved.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel relieved once they respond with understanding about gap years?

Scenario: While talking with a friends, the topic of future kids comes up casually. You feel a sudden heaviness thinking about what the world might look like. You remind yourself you don’t need answers yet, and you feel lighter.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel you need to have all the answers about the future right now?

Scenario: During a long car ride to see relatives, your sibling plays music you don’t like and ignores your comments. You worry speaking up will cause tension for the rest of the trip. When you think about tolerating the discomfort in exchange for change, you feel fine.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel fine tolerating the discomfort to avoid causing tension?

Scenario: At a family dinner, someone mentions rising sea levels, and your stomach twists thinking the coastline you love will vanish. You imagine visiting someday and finding it ruined. You remind yourself that environmental changes are gradual and efforts to protect coastlines are underway.
Comprehension Question: Do you remind yourself that efforts to protect coastlines are underway?

Scenario: Your family goes on a weekend hike at a nearby trail. Early on, you start breathing harder than you expected, and your family slows down so you can catch up. You think your family will be accepting of your differences in pace.
Comprehension Question: Will your family leave you behind on the hike because you're going slower?

Scenario: You and your parent walk back to the car after a tough loss. Your parent is quiet on the drive home, and you slump into the car feeling like you ruined everything. You think your parents silence means they feel sympathy for you.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your parent's silence reflects sympathy rather than anger?

Scenario: You received a poor score on a test, and your guardian must sign off on it because the grade is low. They don't say anything when you show them your test. They are probably feeling unconcerned.
Comprehension Question: Are your guardians probably unconcerned rather than upset about your grade?

Scenario: You don't have internet access at home. You found out that you're required to do a big research project online by next week. As you wonder how you'll be able to complete the assignment, you feel comfortable in your ability to figure it out.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel hopeless about completing the project without home internet?

Scenario: You got caught breaking a rule at school. You didn't mean to, and know that the principal will need to call your parent. You walk into their office, knowing that no matter what happens, your parents will forgive you.
Comprehension Question: Do you know that your parents will forgive you no matter what happens?

Scenario: You and your sibling share a computer. You have an assignment due tonight, but they're using the computer. When you think about asking them to use the computer to finish your homework, you feel optimistic that they will understand.
Comprehension Question: Are you optimistic that your sibling will understand you need the computer?

Scenario: Tonight is the night of parent-teacher conferences. You're not doing well in math, and you know your teacher will tell your parents about your recent grades. When you think about what your parents will say to you afterwards, you know that if they are disappointed, things will turn out okay.
Comprehension Question: Is it normal for parents to be dissappointed sometimes?

Scenario: During dinner with your family, you get compared to your sibling who always gets straight A’s. You feel a twinge of resentment, wondering if you’ll ever measure up. When you mentally compare yourself to your sibling, you acknowledge that you both have different strengths.
Comprehension Question: Do you acknowledge that you and your sibling have different strengths?

Scenario: At dinner, your parents ask to see your and your siblings' report cards. You catch a glance of your sibling’s report card full of A’s and feel inadequate. You remind yourself that everyone’s strengths look different, and you feel capable.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel capable even though your sibling's report card is full of A's?

Scenario: You and your parent are cooking dinner together and talking about your family. Your parent casually mentions how responsible your sibling is. You immediately feel proud of your sibling.
Comprehension Question: Are you proud of your sibling?
